issues.description: None of the nine consumed DTA inputs appears in the frozen package inventory. The datasheet says proprietary data cannot be shared externally, which rules out a public release, but it does not establish whether authorized author/company-controlled access is available. No compatible local route or complete input coverage has been verified.

2_Analysis.do saves its prepared panel before entering Analysen, then issues repeated relative cd "Analysen" commands before reopening that panel. The straight-through producer/consumer paths therefore require reconciliation; preserve the ordered branches and identify a consistent working-directory setup or path correction.

The code names the input keys and many downstream variables, but no DTA schemas or data dictionary are supplied. The source does not establish which merged file supplies several store attributes and employee age, gender and tenure; input field mappings, key populations, and complete date coverage therefore remain unverified. Preserve the authored merge definitions and obtain authorized field/coverage documentation rather than reconstructing the study data.

actions.description: Seek an authorized restricted route to the exact author-prepared study inputs. The datasheet rules out public sharing; it does not establish whether a secure author/company-controlled workspace or execution arrangement can be approved.
steps: Ask the authors or company representative whether an approved secure environment can provide the exact named DTA inputs or run the supplied workflow without externally sharing employee or customer records.
Keep public release and controlled access as separate routes; if no permitted controlled route is available, retain the input as unresolved rather than reconstructing or substituting data.
Do not seek to retrieve proprietary records through Google Analytics or Qualtrics product pages; those pages document product functionality, not the authors’ study exports.
validation: After authorized access, confirm each named input is the same source product and format consumed by the corresponding do-file.
Record only permitted local access conditions and bounded metadata; do not redistribute restricted records.

actions.description: Obtain the missing data dictionaries and coverage descriptions for the nine exact DTA inputs. Keep the authored join definitions and derived variables intact while resolving source-column ownership, identifier units and period coverage.
steps: For 220718 Combined Dataset.dta, map v1-v17 to the source fields the transformation expects and document its employee/store/date units and full required period.
For StoreData and personnel records, identify the fields supplied under idstore and IDEMPLSTNR, including where persnr, age, gender, tenure and the store attributes used in the analysis originate.
For department assignment and both treatment files, document the source columns and population for persnr/idstore and the required assignment variables without changing the supplied merges.
For app usage and work-time records, document employee/week keys, active, hours and absence fields, source periods, and the complete coverage needed by the authored panel.
For QuestShort.dta, map Qualtrics response identifiers, completion/treatment fields and all question columns to the variables named by 3_Survey.do, including numeric-versus-label coding.
validation: After permission is established, use bounded DTA metadata/header probes to check the listed source columns, types and keys; do not use full-file row counts as a coverage proxy.
Compare documented complete date and population coverage with the authored analysis windows and the survey's three-month recall period.
Preserve merge m:1/m:m choices as written; resolve any actual key, field or coverage mismatch from the data dictionary and observed metadata rather than guessing replacements.

actions.description: Configure the eight Stata commands that the supplied source uses but the bounded software probes did not find: winsor2, asdoc, mrtab, stddiff, distinct, pc_simulate, xtqreg and ivreghdfe. Keep Stata 18 and resolve package dependencies through approved sources.
steps: Install or enable each missing command in the Stata 18 adopath using an authorized package source; record package versions and required dependencies, especially for ivreghdfe.
Keep the already found reghdfe, esttab, eststo, unique and coefplot commands available in the same Stata environment.
validation: Run only command lookup/version checks for the required add-ons and record the resolved paths and versions; do not use author data or execute the study programs during setup.

actions.description: Run every supplied branch in order from a clean working copy after authorized inputs, the missing add-ons and the proposed path setup are available. The survey file is a separate input and branch.
steps: Copy the three author do-files and required documentation into a portable working copy; place only authorized exact DTA inputs at their documented paths and keep the original generation/archive files untouched.

From the working-copy project root, run 1_Transform Combined Data to Workfile Dataset.do; it reads 220718 Combined Dataset.dta, STATA/StoreData.dta and personell records stata.dta, then produces 2200718 Workfile Dataset.dta.

From the same root, run the prepared 2_Analysis.do: it reads the generated workfile plus department assignment, prior and current treatment, app-usage and work-time inputs; it produces the collapsed weekly panel, STEP1 panel and analysis-ready panel before the analysis branches.

With the five path edits applied and Analysen present, keep all power, treatment, robustness, compliance, LATE and additional-analysis outputs in that one folder; pc_simulate produces CSVs that the supplied code converts to DTA and appends.
Run 3_Survey.do from a fresh Stata session whose working directory contains QuestShort.dta; it is a separate author-provided survey analysis, not an optional substitute for the transaction panel.
validation: In a future authorized run, record the exact Stata invocation, working directory, return code and raw stdout/stderr; then verify every generated handoff exists before its consumer and each required analysis branch completes.
Compare the produced analysis and survey outputs with the author-documented tables and figures; do not infer completion of any unprovided paper-wide estimator.

review_notes: The frozen title and the datasheet title describe the same paper; the dash punctuation differs typographically only.

The only author-named external platforms are Google Analytics and Qualtrix/Qualtrics, used to produce author-specific data; their official product documentation and exact frozen-catalog names were checked. Those checks do not provide or verify the authors’ private exports.
No author-stated data/code URL appears in the supplied datasheet or appendix; no data, archive, API or account payload was requested.
The public-sharing barrier applies to public release only; authorized restricted access remains unverified.
